We have arrays nums1, nums2 each of length n.

We can perform operations: choose an index i (0 <= i <= n-1) and swap nums1[i] and nums2[i].

Goal: After some number of operations (possibly zero), we want:

- nums1[n-1] is equal to the minimum element in nums1 array (i.e., it must be the minimum among all elements after operations).
- Similarly, nums2[n-1] must equal the minimum among all elements in nums2 array after operations.

We can swap each index arbitrarily many times? Since swapping twice returns to original; each index can be swapped at most once effectively (swap or not), because performing swap twice cancels out. So each index either remains as original or swapped.

Thus we need to decide for each index i whether to swap or not, to achieve the conditions.

But we want the maximum number of operations (i.e., swaps) required to satisfy both conditions. So we want the maximum possible number of indices we swap (subject to being able to satisfy constraints). Equivalent to: find a feasible assignment of swap/not swap to each index such that after applying those swaps, the conditions hold; and maximize total number of swaps.
